findings.text: nothing refreshes a host's beat on an interval, so the 90-second stale window releases a foreign reservation while its holder is still working — the only production publisher is `_publish_reservation_host` at reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2889, called once when a reservation is taken, so a host that takes no new launch for ninety seconds reads as gone to every other host, `reservation_in_flight` returns False, and a second launch on the same attempt is admitted; the constant's own comment claims a window "well above the interval at which anything publishes one" and no such interval exists.

`release_unspawned_reservations` omits the `_reserved_attempt_ended` guard its twin `release_a_withdrawn_reservation` applies at :2861, so it can write an `exit_code: null` receipt over an attempt's real exit record.

`getattr(repair, "supersede_a_held_repair_round", None)` followed by `pytest.skip` turns deletion of the capability the done_when names into a green skip, and :267 and :171 do the same for the withdrawal call and the heartbeat module.
`heartbeat_host` duplicates `local_host`, which reckon/crew/host_lease.py:19 already owns and twelve modules already import.
the loop body repeats `release_a_withdrawn_reservation`'s body at :2839-2877 line for line instead of calling it, so a change to one release path will not reach the other.

the lapsed-beat branch — a beat present but older than HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECONDS at reckon/crew/host_heartbeat.py:31 — is untested, because this case covers only a beat that was never written and reaches its answer by a different comparison.

the gate paragraph rests on two suite logs that match the repository's `*.log` gitignore rule, so they are uncommitted and vanish with the worktree; the copies in the run directory are the ones a later reader can open.

item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a reservation or lock holds only while its holder is working on it; reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2559 `_reservation_holder_running` picks the liveness test per holder, reckon/crew/resumption.py:319 `launch_mark_holds` spends a resume mark once its attempt has answered, and reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:118 lets a door that never launched release what it holds — read in full; the first is only partly faithful, because a holder on another host is judged by when that host last took a launch rather than by whether this holder is still working.
